subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 240 - Management Override of Controls & Journal Entries
question: During the audit of Zenith Steel Ltd., the engagement team notices that the CFO posted several manual journal entries directly to revenue and inventory accounts at 11:45 PM on March 31 without any supporting narration or supervisory approval. Under SA 240 'The Auditor's Responsibilities Relating to Fraud in an Audit of Financial Statements', which specific audit procedure is mandatory to address the risk of management override of controls?
options: Test the appropriateness of journal entries recorded in the general ledger and other adjustments made in the preparation of the financial statements, review accounting estimates for biases, and evaluate the business rationale for significant unusual transactions.
Rely entirely on the written representation letter obtained from the Chief Executive Officer and CFO confirming that all journal entries are legitimate.
Immediately resign from the audit engagement without performing any testing because manual journal entries automatically signify criminal fraud.
Qualify the audit opinion without examining the entries because internal financial controls are deemed to have completely failed.
ref: SA 240, Paragraph 32 - Management Override of Controls
explanation: Under SA 240.32, to address the risk of management override of controls, the auditor is mandatorily required to: (1) Test the appropriateness of journal entries recorded in the general ledger and other adjustments made in the preparation of the financial statements; (2) Review accounting estimates for biases and evaluate whether circumstances producing bias represent risk of material misstatement due to fraud; and (3) Evaluate the business rationale for significant transactions that are outside the normal course of business.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 505 - External Confirmations & Management Refusal
question: In the statutory audit of Omega Pharma Ltd., trade receivables constitute 35% of total assets. The auditor selects 25 high-value debtors for external confirmation under SA 505. Management requests the auditor not to send confirmation requests to 4 major debtors representing 18% of total receivables, citing sensitive commercial renegotiations. What is the auditor's required course of action under SA 505?
options: Inquire into management's reasons for refusal, seek audit evidence regarding validity and reasonableness, evaluate the implications on risk assessment, and perform alternative audit procedures. If refusal is unreasonable and alternative evidence cannot be obtained, communicate with TCWG and modify the opinion.
Accept management's refusal unconditionally as commercial negotiations take precedence over auditing standards.
Automatically issue an adverse opinion without seeking any explanation or performing alternative procedures.
Issue a clean unmodified opinion provided management issues a post-dated cheque for the unconfirmed balances.
ref: SA 505, Paragraphs 8 & 9 - Management's Refusal to Allow the Auditor to Send a Confirmation Request
explanation: Under SA 505.8-9, if management refuses to allow confirmation requests, the auditor must: (a) Inquire as to management's reasons and seek audit evidence as to their validity and reasonableness; (b) Evaluate implications on assessment of relevant risks of material misstatement, including fraud risk; and (c) Perform alternative audit procedures. If the auditor concludes that refusal is unreasonable or is unable to obtain relevant and reliable audit evidence from alternative procedures, the auditor shall communicate with TCWG and determine the implication for the audit and the opinion under SA 705.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 570 (Revised) - Going Concern & Material Uncertainty
question: Kaveri Textiles Ltd. has incurred continuous operating losses for 3 years, its net worth is negative, and working capital is severely negative. However, management has entered into a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with a strategic investor to infuse ₹120 Crores equity subject to regulatory approvals. Management has adequately disclosed the existence of material uncertainty in Note 28 of the financial statements and prepared the statements on a going concern basis. What is the appropriate audit reporting under SA 570 (Revised)?
options: Express an unmodified opinion and include a separate section under the heading 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' drawing attention to Note 28.
Issue an Adverse Opinion because any company with negative net worth cannot prepare accounts on a going concern basis.
Express a Qualified Opinion citing that the MoU is non-binding and regulatory approval is uncertain.
Include the matter strictly as a Key Audit Matter (KAM) under SA 701 and omit the 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' section.
ref: SA 570 (Revised), Paragraphs 22 & 23 - Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern Adequately Disclosed
explanation: Under SA 570 (Revised).22, if adequate disclosure about the material uncertainty is made in the financial statements, the auditor shall express an unmodified opinion and the auditor's report shall include a separate section under the heading 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' to: (a) Draw attention to the note in the financial statements disclosing the matter; and (b) State that these events or conditions indicate a material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on the entity's ability to continue as a going concern and that the auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of the matter.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 299 - Joint Audit Responsibilities & Disagreement
question: CA Raman and CA Suresh are appointed as joint auditors of Bharat Heavy Engineering Ltd. Work is formally allocated between them: Raman is assigned procurement, inventory, and production, while Suresh is assigned sales, treasury, and statutory liabilities. During the audit, Suresh identifies serious discrepancies in treasury investments which Raman believes are immaterial. Suresh insists on modifying the audit report, while Raman wishes to issue an unmodified report. Under SA 299 'Joint Audit of Financial Statements', how should the auditors proceed?
options: The joint auditors are not required to adopt the opinion of the majority. Each joint auditor shall express their own opinion through separate audit reports, cross-referencing the report issued by the other joint auditor.
The opinion of the senior-most auditor (in age or seniority of membership) shall prevail and bind the other auditor.
They must refer the dispute to the Central Council of ICAI and withhold the audit report until ICAI issues a binding ruling.
Raman must sign the report because treasury was allocated to Suresh, so Raman has no right to dissent.
ref: SA 299 (Revised), Paragraph 11 - Disagreement Among Joint Auditors
explanation: Under SA 299 (Revised).11, where the joint auditors are in disagreement with regard to any matters or the opinion to be expressed, they are not bound by the view of the majority. Each joint auditor shall express his own opinion through a separate audit report. A joint auditor is not bound to adopt the majority view and shall issue a separate report, referencing the report issued by the other joint auditor(s).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 550 - Related Parties & Arm's Length Assertion
question: During the audit of Alpha Motors Ltd., the auditor discovers that the company sold commercial vehicles worth ₹45 Crores to an entity controlled by the Managing Director's brother. Management asserts in the notes that the transaction was conducted on terms equivalent to those prevailing in an arm's length transaction. Under SA 550 'Related Parties', what is the auditor's responsibility regarding this management assertion?
options: The auditor must obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to substantiate management's assertion that the transaction was at arm's length. If management cannot support the claim and refuses to remove it, the auditor must modify the audit opinion.
The auditor has no obligation to verify arm's length claims as pricing decisions are purely executive managerial prerogatives.
The auditor can accept the assertion based solely on a written representation letter without corroborative evidence.
The auditor must refer the transaction to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for statutory investigation.
ref: SA 550, Paragraph 24 - Assertions That Related Party Transactions Were Conducted on Arm's Length Terms
explanation: Under SA 550.24, if management makes an assertion in the financial statements that a related party transaction was conducted on terms equivalent to those prevailing in an arm's length transaction, the auditor shall obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the assertion. If the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient evidence to support this assertion, the auditor shall request management to modify the disclosure, and if management refuses, modify the opinion under SA 705.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 560 - Subsequent Events & Amended Financial Statements
question: The audit report of Delta Infra Ltd. for FY 2023-24 was signed on May 15, 2024. On June 10, 2024 (before the financial statements were issued to shareholders), a catastrophic fire destroyed Delta's primary manufacturing facility with an uninsured loss of ₹80 Crores. Management amends the financial statements. The auditor agrees to extend subsequent events procedures to the date of the new audit report. What options does the auditor have regarding the audit report date under SA 560?
options: The auditor can either amend the audit report to include an additional date restricted to that amendment (dual dating) or provide a new or amended audit report with a new date extended to June 10, 2024.
The auditor must retain the original date of May 15, 2024 without mentioning the fire anywhere.
The auditor must resign immediately because the financial statements cannot be altered after signing.
The auditor can only report the matter in CARO 2020 for the subsequent financial year.
ref: SA 560, Paragraphs 11 & 12 - Subsequent Events Occurring Before Issuance of Financial Statements
explanation: Under SA 560.11-12, when management amends the financial statements after the audit report date but before issuance, the auditor shall extend audit procedures to the date of the new report. The auditor can either: (a) Amend the audit report to include an additional date restricted to that amendment (dual dating); or (b) Provide a new or amended auditor's report with a new date, covering all subsequent events up to the new date.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 540 (Revised) - Auditing Accounting Estimates & Fair Value
question: In auditing the expected credit loss (ECL) model under Ind AS 109 of a scheduled commercial bank, the auditor evaluates management's macro-economic forward-looking point estimates. Under SA 540 (Revised) 'Auditing Accounting Estimates and Related Disclosures', which of the following is considered an auditor's independent response when estimation uncertainty is high?
options: Develop an independent point estimate or range to evaluate management's point estimate, and test the operating effectiveness of controls over how management developed the estimate.
Blindly adopt management's internal mathematical model without testing any assumptions.
Request the Reserve Bank of India to audit the ECL model on the auditor's behalf.
Disclaim the opinion automatically because estimation uncertainty is inherently subjective.
ref: SA 540 (Revised), Paragraph 18 - Auditor's Further Substantive Procedures on Accounting Estimates
explanation: Under SA 540 (Revised).18, in responding to the assessed risks of material misstatement for accounting estimates, the auditor's procedures shall include one or more of: (a) Testing how management made the accounting estimate; (b) Testing the operating effectiveness of controls; (c) Developing an auditor's point estimate or range; and (d) Obtaining audit evidence from events occurring up to the date of the auditor's report.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 510 - Initial Audit Engagements & Opening Balances
question: CA Tarun is appointed as statutory auditor of Apex Ltd. for FY 2023-24. The prior year financial statements were audited by another auditor who expressed an unmodified opinion. Under SA 510 'Initial Audit Engagements - Opening Balances', what is Tarun's responsibility regarding opening balances?
options: Read the most recent financial statements and predecessor auditor's report, and obtain sufficient appropriate evidence about whether opening balances contain misstatements that materially affect the current period's financial statements.
Re-audit all prior period transactions from inception of the company.
Rely entirely on the predecessor auditor's report without performing any inquiry or procedures.
Disclaim an opinion on opening balances in the auditor's report for the current year.
ref: SA 510, Paragraph 6 - Audit Procedures Regarding Opening Balances
explanation: Under SA 510.6, the auditor shall obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about whether the opening balances contain misstatements that materially affect the current period's financial statements by: (a) Determining whether the prior period's closing balances have been correctly brought forward; (b) Determining whether the opening balances reflect the application of appropriate accounting policies; and (c) Reviewing the predecessor auditor's working papers or evaluating current period audit procedures.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 501 - Physical Inventory Counting
question: Zenith Retail Ltd. holds physical inventory worth ₹250 Crores across 12 centralized warehouses. Physical verification was conducted by management on March 31, 2024. Due to unforeseen regional lockdowns, the statutory auditor was unable to attend the physical count on that date. What does SA 501 require the auditor to do?
options: Perform physical count observation on an alternative date, and perform audit procedures on intervening transactions to assess whether changes in inventory between the count date and financial statement date are properly recorded.
Issue an immediate disclaimer of opinion without attempting alternative dates or procedures.
Accept management's internal stock register extracts as conclusive evidence.
Instruct management to cancel the financial statements and re-conduct the count after 6 months.
ref: SA 501, Paragraph 5 - Attendance at Physical Inventory Counting on an Alternative Date
explanation: Under SA 501.5, if physical inventory counting is conducted at a date other than the date of the financial statements, or if the auditor is unable to attend due to unforeseen circumstances, the auditor shall perform audit procedures on an alternative date and perform audit procedures on intervening transactions to reconcile changes between count date and balance sheet date.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 580 - Written Representations as Audit Evidence
question: During the audit of Skylark Aviation Ltd., the auditor requests management to provide written representations regarding the completeness of recorded liabilities and title to leased aircraft. The CEO states: 'Since you have verified all records and audit evidence, our written representation is redundant.' What is the conceptual standing of written representations under SA 580?
options: Written representations provide necessary audit evidence, but they do NOT provide sufficient appropriate audit evidence on their own about any of the matters with which they deal, nor do they relieve the auditor of other audit procedures.
Written representations are conclusive evidence that completely replaces the need for substantive audit procedures.
Written representations are purely optional and may be waived at management's discretion.
If written representations are obtained, the auditor cannot be held guilty of professional negligence under any circumstances.
ref: SA 580, Paragraphs 3 & 4 - Nature of Written Representations as Audit Evidence
explanation: SA 580.3-4 makes it clear that although written representations provide necessary audit evidence, they do not provide sufficient appropriate audit evidence on their own about any of the matters with which they deal. Furthermore, the fact that management has provided reliable written representations does not affect the nature or extent of other audit evidence that the auditor must obtain.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 530 - Audit Sampling & Anomaly
question: While testing 100 sample invoices out of a population of 10,000 sales invoices under SA 530, the auditor identifies a pricing error of ₹50,000 on one invoice. Management asserts that this error was caused by a temporary system glitch on a single afternoon and should be classified as an 'anomaly'. How must the auditor treat this error under SA 530?
options: Obtain a high degree of certainty that the misstatement is not representative of the population by performing additional audit procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence that it does not affect the rest of the population.
Accept management's word and exclude the error from population projection automatically.
Double the total sales revenue of the company as punitive projection.
Cancel the sample and declare the entire accounts receivable balance fraudulent.
ref: SA 530, Paragraph 13 - Investigating the Nature and Cause of Deviations and Misstatements (Anomaly)
explanation: Under SA 530.13, when a misstatement has been established as an anomaly, the auditor may exclude it when projecting misstatements to the population. However, to treat a misstatement as an anomaly, the auditor must obtain a high degree of certainty that such misstatement or deviation is not representative of the population by performing additional audit procedures.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 210 - Preconditions for an Audit & Limitation of Scope
question: Prior to accepting the audit engagement of Matrix Infotech Ltd., management insists that the audit report must exclude any examination of intellectual property valuations and offshore subsidiary transfers. Under SA 210 'Agreeing the Terms of Audit Engagements', what must the auditor do?
options: Do not accept the engagement if management imposes a limitation on scope such that the auditor believes the limitation will result in disclaiming an opinion, unless required by law.
Accept the engagement and agree to management's clauses in the engagement letter without objection.
Accept the engagement and immediately charge triple the audit fee.
Accept the engagement and sign an NDA promising never to report the limitation to shareholders.
ref: SA 210, Paragraph 7 - Limitation on Scope Prior to Audit Engagement Acceptance
explanation: Under SA 210.7, if management or TCWG impose a limitation on the scope of the auditor's work in the terms of a proposed audit engagement such that the auditor believes the limitation will result in the auditor disclaiming an opinion on the financial statements, the auditor shall not accept such a limited engagement as an audit engagement, unless required by law or regulation to do so.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 250 - Consideration of Laws and Regulations (NOCLAR)
question: During the audit of a chemical manufacturer, the auditor discovers unauthorized dumping of toxic effluents in violation of environmental laws punishable by closure of plant and heavy penalties. Management argues that environmental laws are non-financial and outside the auditor's scope. Under SA 250, what are the auditor's categories of laws and regulations?
options: Category 1: Laws having a direct effect on determination of material amounts and disclosures in financial statements; Category 2: Other laws that may not have direct effect but compliance with which is fundamental to operating aspects, going concern, or avoiding material penalties.
All laws are outside the auditor's scope unless specifically audited by the Government.
The auditor is only responsible for the Income Tax Act and Companies Act; environmental laws can never affect financial statements.
The auditor must arrest the factory manager under statutory citizen powers.
ref: SA 250 (Revised), Paragraph 6 - Categories of Laws and Regulations
explanation: SA 250.6 distinguishes the auditor's responsibilities into two categories: (a) Provisions of laws and regulations generally recognized to have a direct effect on the determination of material amounts and disclosures in the financial statements (e.g. tax laws); and (b) Other laws and regulations that do not have a direct effect, but compliance with which may be fundamental to operating aspects of the business, its ability to continue as a going concern, or to avoid material penalties (e.g. environmental compliance).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 260 - Communication with TCWG
question: Under SA 260 (Revised) 'Communication with Those Charged with Governance', which of the following matters is the auditor MANDATORILY required to communicate to TCWG in the audit of a listed entity?
options: The auditor's responsibilities, planned scope and timing of the audit, significant findings including accounting policies and estimates, significant difficulties encountered, and a written statement confirming auditor independence.
Daily working hours of audit trainees and the firm's detailed cost breakdown.
The names of whistle-blowers who provided confidential tips to the audit team.
The personal tax returns of all members of the audit engagement team.
ref: SA 260 (Revised), Paragraphs 14-17 - Matters to be Communicated to TCWG
explanation: Under SA 260 (Revised).14-17, the auditor shall communicate: (1) Auditor's responsibilities in relation to financial statements; (2) Planned scope and timing of audit; (3) Significant findings from the audit (accounting policies, accounting estimates, significant difficulties); and (4) For listed entities, auditor independence, including a statement that the engagement team has complied with relevant ethical requirements regarding independence.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 520 - Substantive Analytical Procedures
question: When designing and performing substantive analytical procedures under SA 520, which factor most critically determines the suitability of analytical procedures as a substantive test?
options: The predictability of the relationship, the availability and reliability of the data, the precision of the expectation developed by the auditor, and the acceptable threshold of difference without further investigation.
The physical proximity of the auditor's office to the client's registered office.
Whether the client uses the same brand of enterprise resource software as the audit firm.
The total amount of statutory audit fee paid by the company.
ref: SA 520, Paragraph 5 - Substantive Analytical Procedures Design
explanation: Under SA 520.5, when designing substantive analytical procedures, the auditor shall: (a) Determine the suitability of particular substantive analytical procedures; (b) Evaluate the reliability of data from which the expectation is developed; (c) Develop an expectation of recorded amounts or ratios; and (d) Determine the amount of any difference of recorded amounts from expected values that is acceptable without further investigation.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 230 - Retention Period of Audit Documentation
question: Under SQC 1 and SA 230 'Audit Documentation', what is the mandatory retention period for audit documentation working paper files for an audit engagement?
options: No shorter than 7 years from the date of the auditor's report (or group auditor's report, if later).
Strictly 3 years from the date of the annual general meeting.
10 years for private companies and 2 years for listed entities.
Until the client's next income tax assessment order is passed.
ref: SQC 1, Paragraph 83 & SA 230, Paragraph A23 - Retention Period for Engagement Documentation
explanation: Under SQC 1.83 and SA 230.A23, the retention period for audit engagements is ordinarily not shorter than seven years from the date of the auditor's report, or if later, the date of the group auditor's report. (Note: Under Section 128(5) of Companies Act 2013, books of account are preserved for 8 years, but SQC 1 mandates at least 7 years for audit files).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 220 (Revised) - Engagement Quality Reviewer Responsibilities
question: Under SA 220 (Revised) 'Quality Management for an Audit of Financial Statements', prior to dating the auditor's report, what specific condition must be satisfied regarding the Engagement Quality Review (EQR)?
options: The engagement partner shall not date the auditor's report until the engagement quality reviewer has notified the engagement partner that the engagement quality review is complete.
The engagement partner can date and issue the report, provided the EQR signs off within 60 days post-issuance.
The engagement quality reviewer must personally visit every branch and factory of the audit client.
The EQR can only be conducted by a retired High Court judge.
ref: SA 220 (Revised), Paragraph 36 - Completion of the Engagement Quality Review
explanation: Under SA 220 (Revised).36, the engagement partner shall not date the auditor's report until notification has been received from the engagement quality reviewer that the engagement quality review is complete in accordance with relevant professional standards.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 265 - Communicating Deficiencies in Internal Control
question: During the audit of a listed entity, the auditor identifies a significant deficiency in internal control over inventory dispatch authorization that creates an opportunity for asset misappropriation. Under SA 265, what is the auditor's reporting obligation?
options: Communicate in writing significant deficiencies in internal control identified during the audit to Those Charged With Governance on a timely basis.
Report the deficiency exclusively to the local police department within 24 hours.
Refuse to issue an audit report until management dismisses the dispatch manager.
Deficiencies in internal control are strictly confidential and cannot be communicated in writing.
ref: SA 265, Paragraph 9 - Communication of Significant Deficiencies to TCWG
explanation: Under SA 265.9, the auditor shall communicate in writing significant deficiencies in internal control identified during the audit to Those Charged With Governance on a timely basis, along with an explanation of their potential effects and sufficient information to enable TCWG to understand the context.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 500 - Reliability of Audit Evidence Hierarchy
question: Under SA 500 'Audit Evidence', which of the following generalizations regarding the reliability of audit evidence is INCORRECT?
options: Audit evidence obtained directly by the auditor is less reliable than audit evidence obtained indirectly or by inference from entity personnel.
The reliability of audit evidence is increased when it is obtained from independent sources outside the entity.
Audit evidence in documentary form (paper or electronic) is more reliable than evidence obtained orally.
Audit evidence provided by original documents is more reliable than audit evidence provided by photocopies or facsimiles.
ref: SA 500, Paragraph A31 - Generalizations About Reliability of Audit Evidence
explanation: Option A is INCORRECT (and hence the correct answer) because SA 500.A31 states that audit evidence obtained directly by the auditor (such as observation of the application of a control) is MORE reliable than audit evidence obtained indirectly or by inference (such as inquiry about the application of a control).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Standards on Auditing (SA) and the Audit Process
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 200 - Professional Skepticism & Inherent Limitations
question: An auditor maintains professional skepticism throughout the audit. Under SA 200, which of the following correctly describes 'professional skepticism' and why an audit cannot provide absolute assurance?
options: Professional skepticism is an attitude that includes a questioning mind, being alert to conditions indicating possible misstatement, and critical assessment of audit evidence; absolute assurance is impossible due to inherent limitations of an audit (nature of financial reporting, nature of audit procedures, and need to conduct audit within a reasonable period and cost).
Professional skepticism means presuming management is guilty of fraud until proven innocent beyond reasonable doubt.
Absolute assurance is achieved whenever the auditor tests 100% of journal entries.
Professional skepticism requires the auditor to challenge and reject all accounting standards.
ref: SA 200, Paragraphs 13(l), 15 & A45 - Professional Skepticism & Inherent Limitations of Audit
explanation: Under SA 200.13(l) & 15, professional skepticism is an attitude that includes a questioning mind, being alert to conditions which may indicate possible misstatement due to error or fraud, and a critical assessment of audit evidence. Absolute assurance is not attainable because of the inherent limitations of an audit: (1) The nature of financial reporting; (2) The nature of audit procedures; and (3) The need for the audit to be conducted within a reasonable period of time and at a reasonable cost.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 315 (Revised) - Five Components of Internal Control
question: In identifying and assessing the risks of material misstatement under SA 315 (Revised), the auditor must obtain an understanding of the entity's internal control system. Which of the following correctly lists the five interrelated components of internal control recognized by SA 315?
options: Control Environment, Entity's Risk Assessment Process, Entity's Process to Monitor the System of Internal Control, Information System and Communication, and Control Activities.
Board Approval, External Legal Opinions, Tax Planning, Statutory Filings, and Shareholder Relations.
Budgeting, Payroll Processing, Fixed Asset Register, Cash Safeguarding, and Vendor Onboarding.
Preventive Controls, Detective Controls, Corrective Controls, Compensating Controls, and Directive Controls.
ref: SA 315 (Revised), Paragraphs 21-27 - Components of System of Internal Control
explanation: Under SA 315 (Revised), the auditor obtains an understanding of the entity's system of internal control across five components: (1) Control Environment; (2) Entity's Risk Assessment Process; (3) Entity's Process to Monitor the System of Internal Control; (4) Information System and Communication; and (5) Control Activities.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 320 - Materiality & Performance Materiality
question: For the audit of Apex Consumer Goods Ltd. (Turnover ₹1,200 Crores, Profit Before Tax ₹60 Crores), the auditor determines Financial Statement Materiality at ₹3 Crores (5% of PBT). To reduce the probability that aggregate uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceed materiality, the auditor sets Performance Materiality at ₹2.1 Crores (70% of materiality). What is the conceptual distinction between Materiality and Performance Materiality under SA 320?
options: Materiality is determined for the financial statements as a whole based on user needs, whereas Performance Materiality is set by the auditor at a lower amount to provide a safety margin against aggregation risk during audit testing.
Performance Materiality is only used for tax computation, while Materiality is used for legal disputes.
Performance Materiality must always be exactly equal to double the overall materiality.
Materiality is set by management in the Board meeting, whereas Performance Materiality is set by ICAI.
ref: SA 320, Paragraphs 9 & 11 - Performance Materiality and Materiality for the Financial Statements as a Whole
explanation: Under SA 320.9 & 11, Performance Materiality means the amount or amounts set by the auditor at less than materiality for the financial statements as a whole to reduce to an appropriately low level the probability that the aggregate of uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceeds materiality for the financial statements as a whole.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Section 143(3)(i) - Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting (IFC-FR)
question: Under Section 143(3)(i) of the Companies Act, 2013, the auditor's report must state whether the company has adequate internal financial controls with reference to financial statements (IFC-FR) and the operating effectiveness of such controls. Which class of private companies is EXEMPT from this requirement under MCA Notification dated June 13, 2017?
options: A private company which is a one person company (OPC) or small company, or a private company having turnover less than ₹50 Crores as per latest audited financial statement AND aggregate borrowings from banks/FIs/bodies corporate less than ₹25 Crores at any time during the financial year.
All private companies are unconditionally exempt regardless of turnover or borrowing levels.
Only private companies with turnover exceeding ₹500 Crores are exempt.
No company in India is exempt from Section 143(3)(i).
ref: MCA Notification G.S.R. 583(E) dated 13th June 2017 - Exemption to Private Companies u/s 143(3)(i)
explanation: Under MCA Notification dated 13th June 2017, the reporting requirement on IFC-FR under Section 143(3)(i) shall not apply to a private company which: (a) Is a one person company (OPC) or a small company; OR (b) Has turnover less than ₹50 Crores as per latest audited financial statements AND aggregate borrowings from banks or financial institutions or any body corporate less than ₹25 Crores at any point of time during the financial year.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 330 - The Auditor's Responses to Assessed Risks
question: Under SA 330 'The Auditor's Responses to Assessed Risks', when the auditor's assessment of risks of material misstatement at the assertion level includes an expectation that internal controls are operating effectively, what is the auditor REQUIRED to do?
options: Design and perform tests of controls to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the operating effectiveness of relevant controls.
Rely on management's verbal reassurance and eliminate all substantive testing.
Eliminate tests of controls and perform 100% substantive vouchers audit.
Issue a clean report without testing controls or transactions.
ref: SA 330, Paragraph 8 - Tests of Controls Requirement
explanation: Under SA 330.8, the auditor shall design and perform tests of controls to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence as to the operating effectiveness of relevant controls if: (a) The auditor's assessment of risks of material misstatement at the assertion level includes an expectation that the controls are operating effectively; or (b) Substantive procedures alone cannot provide sufficient appropriate audit evidence at the assertion level.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 402 - Audit Considerations Relating to Service Organizations
question: Pinnacle Mutual Fund outsources its registrar and transfer agency (RTA) operations, unit capital accounting, and NAV calculations to CAMS Ltd. Under SA 402, Pinnacle's statutory auditor wants to obtain audit evidence regarding internal controls at CAMS. Which type of independent assurance report provided by CAMS's service auditor provides evidence regarding both the suitability of design AND the operating effectiveness of controls?
options: Type 2 report (Report on the description, design, and operating effectiveness of controls at a service organization throughout a specified period).
Type 1 report (Report on description and design of controls as at a specific date only).
A general character certificate issued by the local chamber of commerce.
A limited review report under SRE 2410.
ref: SA 402, Paragraph 8 & SAE 3402 - Type 1 vs Type 2 Service Auditor Reports
explanation: Under SA 402.8 and SAE 3402, a Type 2 report comprises a report by the service auditor on the description, design, AND operating effectiveness of controls at the service organization throughout a specified period. A Type 1 report only covers description and design suitability as at a specified date, without testing operating effectiveness.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 450 - Evaluation of Misstatements Identified During Audit
question: During the audit of a construction company, the auditor discovers uncorrected misstatements totaling ₹4.2 Crores. Overall materiality is ₹5 Crores. Management refuses to adjust the errors arguing they are below materiality. Under SA 450, how should the auditor evaluate these uncorrected misstatements before forming an opinion?
options: Reassess materiality, determine whether uncorrected misstatements are material individually or in aggregate (considering their size and nature, and the particular circumstances of their occurrence), and request written representations from management regarding their immateriality.
Conclude automatically that since ₹4.2 Cr is below ₹5 Cr, no further evaluation or inquiry is required.
Force management to increase revenue by ₹4.2 Crores to balance the error.
Resign immediately without communicating with the Audit Committee.
ref: SA 450, Paragraphs 10, 11 & 14 - Evaluating the Effect of Uncorrected Misstatements
explanation: Under SA 450.10-14, the auditor shall determine whether uncorrected misstatements are material, individually or in aggregate. In making this determination, the auditor shall consider: (a) The size and nature of the misstatements, both in relation to particular classes of transactions and financial statements as a whole; and (b) The effect of uncorrected misstatements related to prior periods. The auditor must also request written representations from management and TCWG whether they believe the effects of uncorrected misstatements are immaterial.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 300 - Overall Audit Strategy vs Audit Plan
question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Overall Audit Strategy from the Detailed Audit Plan under SA 300 'Planning an Audit of Financial Statements'?
options: The audit strategy sets the scope, timing, and direction of the audit and guides the development of the audit plan; the audit plan is more detailed and includes the nature, timing, and extent of risk assessment procedures, further audit procedures at assertion level, and other planned audit procedures.
The audit plan is prepared first by the client, and the audit strategy is developed later by the auditor.
The audit strategy is legally binding on shareholders, while the audit plan can never be updated once written.
There is no distinction between audit strategy and audit plan; they are identical documents.
ref: SA 300, Paragraphs 7, 8 & 9 - Audit Strategy and Audit Plan
explanation: Under SA 300.7-9, the auditor shall establish an overall audit strategy that sets the scope, timing, and direction of the audit, and that guides the development of the audit plan. The audit plan is more detailed than the overall audit strategy in that it includes the nature, timing, and extent of audit procedures to be performed by engagement team members (risk assessment procedures and further audit procedures at assertion level).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 315 - Significant Risks Identification
question: Under SA 315 (Revised), what is defined as a 'Significant Risk' and what mandatory audit response is required under SA 330?
options: An identified risk of material misstatement for which the assessment of inherent risk is close to the upper end of the spectrum of inherent risk; for significant risks, the auditor cannot rely on controls tested in prior years and must perform substantive procedures that are specifically responsive to that risk (including tests of details).
Any risk where the value involved is greater than ₹1 Lakh.
A risk that only arises during foreign currency conversions.
A risk where management refuses to sign the balance sheet.
ref: SA 315 (Revised), Paragraph 12(l) & SA 330, Paragraphs 15 & 21 - Significant Risks Definition & Audit Response
explanation: Under SA 315.12(l), a significant risk is an identified risk of material misstatement for which the assessment of inherent risk is close to the upper end of the spectrum. Under SA 330.15 & 21, when the auditor plans to rely on controls over a significant risk, the auditor shall test those controls in the current period (no multi-year reliance) and shall perform substantive procedures that are specifically responsive to that risk (which must include tests of details if only substantive procedures are applied).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Internal Control - Segregation of Duties (SoD) Conflict
question: In review of the revenue cycle of Nova Logistics Ltd., the auditor observes that the senior accountant has access rights in SAP ERP to create new customer accounts, generate sales orders, approve credit limits, record journal entries, and issue credit notes. Which core internal control concept is severely compromised here?
options: Segregation of Duties (SoD) — custody of assets, authorization of transactions, execution, and recording should be separated among different individuals to prevent and detect errors or fraud in the normal course of duties.
Principle of double-entry bookkeeping.
Prudence and conservatism principle under Ind AS 1.
Going concern assumption.
ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting - Segregation of Duties
explanation: Segregation of Duties (SoD) is a fundamental internal control concept where no single individual should be in a position to perpetrate and conceal errors or fraud in the normal course of their duties. Combining authorization (credit approval), recording (sales ledger & journal entries), and execution (issuing credit notes) creates a critical SoD conflict.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 315 - Scalability & Understanding IT Environment
question: Under SA 315 (Revised), in understanding the entity's IT environment, what are General IT Controls (GITCs) and why are they evaluated by the auditor?
options: GITCs are controls over the entity's IT processes that support the continued proper operation of the IT environment, including programs, data integrity, and operations (access security, program changes, computer operations); they are evaluated because deficiencies in GITCs can undermine automated application controls.
GITCs refer solely to the warranty certificates of laptops used by directors.
GITCs are controls exercised by the internet service provider outside the client's premises.
GITCs are only applicable when an entity develops its own commercial video games.
ref: SA 315 (Revised), Appendix 5 - Understanding Information Technology and General IT Controls
explanation: Under SA 315 (Revised) Appendix 5, General IT Controls (GITCs) are controls over the entity's IT processes that support the continued proper operation of the IT environment, including access to programs and data, program change management, and computer operations. Effective GITCs provide assurance that automated application controls and IT-dependent manual controls operate consistently as designed.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 330 - Rotational Testing of Controls
question: Under SA 330, if the auditor plans to rely on controls over an assertion that has NOT changed since they were last tested, how frequently must the auditor test the operating effectiveness of such controls?
options: The auditor shall test the controls at least once in every third audit, and shall test some controls in each audit to avoid testing all controls in a single period.
The auditor never needs to test controls again once they are tested during initial engagement.
The auditor must test all controls every single month.
Controls can be relied on indefinitely provided the IT manager signs a certificate.
ref: SA 330, Paragraph 14(b) - Testing Controls on a Rotational Basis
explanation: Under SA 330.14(b), if the auditor plans to rely on controls that have not changed since they were last tested, the auditor shall test the operating effectiveness of such controls at least once in every third audit, and shall test some controls each audit to avoid the possibility of testing all controls in a single audit period and no controls in the subsequent two periods.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Audit Risk Model - Inherent Risk & Control Risk
question: Under the classical Audit Risk model: Audit Risk (AR) = Inherent Risk (IR) × Control Risk (CR) × Detection Risk (DR). If the auditor evaluates Inherent Risk as High and Control Risk as High (meaning Risk of Material Misstatement is High), what level of Detection Risk must the auditor accept, and what are the implications for audit procedures?
options: The auditor must set acceptable Detection Risk at a Low level, requiring more extensive, effective substantive procedures, performed closer to the period-end, with larger sample sizes.
The auditor can set Detection Risk at High, reducing audit testing to save time.
Detection Risk is fixed by statute at 50% and cannot be adjusted by the auditor.
The auditor must accept that Audit Risk will automatically be 100% and issue an adverse opinion.
ref: SA 200, Paragraph A38 & SA 315 - Audit Risk Components & Inversely Related Detection Risk
explanation: Under the Audit Risk Model, Detection Risk is inversely related to the assessed Risk of Material Misstatement (IR × CR). When RMM is High, acceptable Detection Risk must be Low in order to keep overall Audit Risk at an acceptably low level. A lower acceptable detection risk requires more persuasive audit evidence, testing closer to year-end, and larger sample sizes.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Walk-Through Tests in Internal Control Evaluation
question: What is the primary objective of performing a 'walk-through test' during the auditor's understanding of internal controls under SA 315?
options: To trace a single transaction through the entire accounting system from initiation to recording and reporting, confirming the auditor's understanding of the transaction flow and identifying points where misstatements could occur.
To verify whether company employees arrive on time at the office.
To physically walk through all manufacturing premises to count laborers.
To verify the market capitalization of the company on the stock exchange.
ref: SA 315 (Revised), Paragraph A129 - Performing Walk-Through Tests
explanation: A walk-through test involves tracing a transaction from its origination through the entity's processes and information systems until it is reflected in the financial reports. Its purpose is to confirm the auditor's understanding of system design, verify whether controls have been implemented, and identify points where material misstatements could occur.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Benchmarking Strategy for Automated Controls
question: Under ICAI Guidance on Audit in an Automated Environment, what is the 'Benchmarking Strategy' for automated application controls?
options: If General IT Controls (especially program change controls and access controls) are effective, an automated application control that was thoroughly tested in a prior period and has remained unchanged can be benchmarked and does not need to be retested every year.
Comparing the client's profit margins against industry leaders like Reliance and Tata.
Testing the speed of the client's broadband connection against international benchmarks.
Benchmarking the CFO's salary against listed industry peers.
ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Internal Financial Controls - Benchmarking Automated Application Controls
explanation: In an automated environment, if General IT Controls (particularly change management and access security) continue to operate effectively and the program code of an automated control has not been modified since it was last tested, the auditor can use a benchmarking strategy—relying on the automated control without re-performing detailed testing of the control logic each year.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Compensating Controls & Deficiencies
question: During control evaluation of a mid-sized branch, the auditor notices that the branch manager personally signs cheques without dual authorization. However, daily bank reconciliation statements are prepared by an independent central treasury team and reviewed weekly by the internal audit team. What is the technical term for the central treasury control in relation to the branch authorization deficiency?
options: Compensating Control — a control that mitigates the risk of a material misstatement arising from a design or operating deficiency in another control.
Preventive Authorization Control.
Inherent Deficiency Control.
Statutory Exemption Control.
ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls - Compensating Controls
explanation: A compensating control is a control that limits the severity of a deficiency and prevents it from rising to the level of a significant deficiency or material weakness. Here, independent daily reconciliation and central review act as a compensating control mitigating the lack of dual cheque signatories at the branch.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SA 320 - Revision of Materiality During Audit
question: The statutory auditor of Zenith Infrastructure Ltd. initially determined materiality at ₹10 Crores based on budgeted revenue of ₹2,000 Crores. During year-end procedures, it is discovered that due to cancellation of two major government contracts, actual revenue dropped to ₹1,100 Crores and actual profit declined by 60%. Under SA 320, what is the auditor REQUIRED to do?
options: Revise materiality (and performance materiality) for the financial statements as a whole, evaluate whether the nature, timing, and extent of further audit procedures remain appropriate, and perform additional procedures as necessary.
Retain the initial ₹10 Crore materiality because materiality cannot be revised once the audit plan is signed.
Automatically qualify the audit report citing that management failed to achieve its revenue budget.
Increase materiality to ₹20 Crores to ensure all errors remain immaterial.
ref: SA 320, Paragraphs 12 & 13 - Revision as the Audit Progresses
explanation: Under SA 320.12-13, the auditor shall revise materiality for the financial statements as a whole (and performance materiality) in the event of becoming aware of information during the audit that would have caused the auditor to have determined a different amount initially. If materiality is revised to a lower amount, the auditor shall determine whether it is necessary to revise performance materiality and whether further audit procedures remain appropriate.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Substantive Testing - Timing of Procedures
question: Under SA 330, when substantive procedures are performed at an intermediate date (e.g. 2 months prior to the balance sheet date), how must the auditor address the remaining period until balance sheet date?
options: Perform substantive procedures, combined with tests of controls for the intervening period, or perform further substantive procedures only, to provide a reasonable basis for extending audit conclusions from the interim date to the period-end.
Assume that balances at period-end are identical to interim balances without further procedures.
Refuse to sign the report unless the client prepares full balance sheets every week.
Resign from the engagement as interim testing is strictly forbidden under Standards on Auditing.
ref: SA 330, Paragraph 22 - Performing Substantive Procedures at an Interim Date
explanation: Under SA 330.22, if substantive procedures are performed at an interim date, the auditor shall cover the remaining period by performing: (a) Substantive procedures, combined with tests of controls for the intervening period; or (b) If the auditor determines that it is sufficient, further substantive procedures only, that provide a reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions from the interim date to the period-end.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] COSO Framework - Monitoring Activities
question: Under the COSO Internal Control Integrated Framework, which of the following represents an ongoing monitoring activity rather than a separate evaluation?
options: Supervisory review of daily cash reconciliations, customer complaint trends, and monthly operational variance reports by operating managers as part of normal recurring operations.
A once-in-five-years comprehensive audit conducted by an external international consulting firm.
A statutory tax audit conducted under Section 44AB of the Income Tax Act.
A peer review conducted by the ICAI Peer Review Board.
ref: COSO Internal Control Integrated Framework - Component 5: Monitoring Activities
explanation: Under the COSO Framework, monitoring activities are divided into: (1) Ongoing evaluations built into business processes at different levels of the entity (e.g. managerial review of operating reports, supervisory reconciliations); and (2) Separate evaluations conducted periodically by internal audit or external experts.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Risk Assessment - Spectrum of Inherent Risk
question: Under SA 315 (Revised), inherent risk factors include complexity, subjectivity, change, uncertainty, or susceptibility to misstatement due to management bias or other fraud risk factors. How does the auditor locate an assertion on the 'spectrum of inherent risk'?
options: By assessing the intersection of the likelihood of a misstatement occurring and the magnitude of the potential misstatement if it were to occur.
By multiplying the number of employees by the turnover of the company.
By assessing the distance of the client's factory from the national capital.
By calculating the P/E ratio of the company on the stock exchange.
ref: SA 315 (Revised), Paragraph 12(l) & Paragraph A207 - Spectrum of Inherent Risk
explanation: Under SA 315 (Revised).A207, in assessing inherent risk for identified risks of material misstatement at the assertion level, the auditor assesses where on the spectrum of inherent risk the risk is located, by considering the degree to which inherent risk factors affect susceptibility to misstatement, which involves assessing the likelihood and magnitude of a potential misstatement.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit Planning, Risk Assessment, and Internal Control Evaluation
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] IT Application Controls - Three-Way Matching
question: In an ERP procurement cycle, an automated control programmatically verifies that the vendor's purchase invoice price and quantity match the Purchase Order (PO) and Goods Receipt Note (GRN) before releasing the payment voucher. If quantity exceeds tolerance of 1%, payment is blocked. What type of control is this?
options: Automated Application Control (Three-Way Match).
Manual Detective Compensating Control.
Environmental IT Infrastructure Control.
Physical Custody Control.
ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Audit in Automated Environment - Automated Application Controls
explanation: Automated application controls are controls embedded within business software applications that automatically prevent or detect unauthorized or erroneous transactions. A programmatic three-way match between PO, GRN, and vendor invoice is a quintessential automated application control.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Bank Audit - NPA Classification Norms (90-Day Overdue)
question: In the statutory branch audit of a Scheduled Commercial Bank as of March 31, 2024, a cash credit account of M/s Pragati Agro Ltd. shows an outstanding balance of ₹4.80 Crores against a sanctioned limit of ₹4.50 Crores. During the quarter ended March 31, 2024, total credits in the account were ₹12 Lakhs, whereas interest debited was ₹16 Lakhs. The account has remained continuously in excess of the sanctioned limit for 95 days. What is the asset classification of this account under RBI Prudential Norms?
options: Non-Performing Asset (NPA) — classified as Substandard Asset because the account is 'out of order' (outstanding balance remained continuously in excess of sanctioned limit for more than 90 days and credits were insufficient to cover interest debited).
Standard Asset, because total turnover of the borrower exceeds ₹50 Crores.
Special Mention Account - 0 (SMA-0), because overdue period is below 180 days.
Loss Asset, requiring immediate 100% write-off.
ref: RBI Master Circular - Prudential Norms on Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning (IRACP)
explanation: Under RBI IRACP norms, a Cash Credit/Overdraft account is treated as NPA if it is 'out of order'. An account is treated as out of order if the outstanding balance remains continuously in excess of the sanctioned limit/drawing power for 90 days, or if credits during the quarter are not enough to cover interest debited. Here, it exceeded limits for 95 days and credits (₹12L) were less than interest (₹16L); hence it must be classified as an NPA (Substandard Asset).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Bank Audit - Provisioning Percentages for Substandard & Doubtful Assets
question: A bank advance of ₹100 Lakhs was classified as Doubtful Asset - Category 2 (Doubtful for more than 1 year and up to 3 years) as on March 31, 2024. The realizable value of tangible security held is ₹60 Lakhs (verified by an approved valuer within the last 3 years). What is the mandatory RBI provisioning required for this asset?
options: Total provision ₹64 Lakhs (100% on unsecured portion ₹40L = ₹40L, plus 40% on secured portion ₹60L = ₹24L).
Total provision ₹100 Lakhs (100% on total advance).
Total provision ₹25 Lakhs (25% on total advance).
Total provision ₹40 Lakhs (only on the unsecured portion).
ref: RBI Master Circular on IRACP - Provisioning Norms for Doubtful Assets (D2)
explanation: For Doubtful Assets Category 2 (D2 - doubtful for >1 year and up to 3 years): (1) Unsecured portion (where realisable value of security is nil) attracts 100% provision: (100 - 60) × 100% = ₹40 Lakhs; (2) Secured portion attracts 40% provision: ₹60L × 40% = ₹24 Lakhs. Total Provision = ₹40L + ₹24L = ₹64 Lakhs.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Bank Audit - Drawing Power (DP) Calculation
question: A borrower is sanctioned a working capital Cash Credit limit of ₹200 Lakhs against hypothecation of stocks and book debts. As on March 31, 2024, stock value is ₹250 Lakhs (including unpaid stock under letter of credit of ₹50 Lakhs and obsolete stock of ₹20 Lakhs). Eligible trade debtors are ₹80 Lakhs (excluding debts older than 90 days). The margin stipulated by the bank is 25% on paid stock and 40% on debtors. What is the Drawing Power (DP) for the borrower?
options: Drawing Power = ₹183 Lakhs (Paid stock ₹180L - 25% margin = ₹135L; Debtors ₹80L - 40% margin = ₹48L; Total = ₹183 Lakhs).
Drawing Power = ₹200 Lakhs (Sanctioned limit is automatically the Drawing Power).
Drawing Power = ₹247.5 Lakhs (Total stock ₹250L + Debtors ₹80L less margins).
Drawing Power = ₹150 Lakhs (Flat 75% of sanctioned limit).
ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Audit of Banks - Verification of Advances & Drawing Power
explanation: Eligible Stock = Gross Stock (₹250L) - Unpaid LC Stock (₹50L) - Obsolete Stock (₹20L) = ₹180 Lakhs. DP on Stock = 180 × (1 - 0.25) = ₹135 Lakhs. Eligible Debtors = ₹80 Lakhs. DP on Debtors = 80 × (1 - 0.40) = ₹48 Lakhs. Total Drawing Power = 135 + 48 = ₹183 Lakhs. (Since DP of ₹183L is less than sanctioned limit of ₹200L, the borrower can draw up to ₹183 Lakhs).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Bank Audit - Basel III CRAR & Capital Adequacy
question: Under RBI Basel III capital adequacy guidelines, what is the minimum regulatory Total Capital Adequacy Ratio (CRAR) and minimum Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio that scheduled commercial banks in India are required to maintain (excluding Capital Conservation Buffer)?
options: Minimum Total CRAR of 9.0% and minimum CET1 ratio of 5.5% of Risk-Weighted Assets (RWAs).
Minimum Total CRAR of 12.0% and minimum CET1 ratio of 8.0%.
Minimum Total CRAR of 8.0% and minimum CET1 ratio of 4.5% (Basel international norm without RBI enhancement).
Minimum Total CRAR of 15.0% for all public and private banks.
ref: RBI Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations
explanation: Under RBI Basel III regulations for commercial banks in India (which are more stringent than the Basel Committee norms): Minimum Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) is 5.5% (vs Basel III global 4.5%); Minimum Tier 1 capital is 7.0%; and Minimum Total Capital (CRAR) is 9.0% (vs Basel III global 8.0%) of Risk-Weighted Assets, plus Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB) of 2.5% in Common Equity Tier 1.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Bank Audit - Long Form Audit Report (LFAR)
question: What is the purpose and structural deadline of the Long Form Audit Report (LFAR) prepared by statutory branch auditors and statutory central auditors of a bank?
options: The LFAR is a comprehensive questionnaire formulated by RBI seeking detailed comments on credit appraisal, sanctioning, monitoring, asset classification, internal controls, fraud, and large advances; it must be submitted to the bank's management and board within the timeline prescribed by RBI (typically by April 30).
The LFAR is a secret document submitted exclusively to the Income Tax Department to compute MAT.
The LFAR replaces the independent auditor's report under the Banking Regulation Act.
The LFAR is only required if a bank suffers a net loss exceeding ₹1,000 Crores.
ref: RBI Circular on Revised LFAR Formats & ICAI Guidance Note on Bank Audit
explanation: The LFAR is a structured questionnaire designed by the RBI requiring statutory branch and central auditors to provide detailed findings and qualitative evaluations on advances, cash management, clearing differences, compliance with RBI circulars, NPA identification, and internal control effectiveness.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Insurance Audit - Solvency Margin Requirement (IRDAI)
question: Under IRDAI (Assets, Liabilities, and Solvency Margin of General Insurance Business) Regulations, what is the mandatory Minimum Solvency Ratio (Control Level of Solvency) that every insurer must maintain at all times?
options: A Solvency Ratio of not less than 1.50 (150% of the Required Solvency Margin).
A Solvency Ratio of not less than 1.00 (100%).
A Solvency Ratio of 2.50 for life insurers and 0.80 for general insurers.
Solvency margins are purely advisory and have no regulatory mandate.
ref: IRDAI Regulations & Section 64VA of Insurance Act, 1938 - Solvency Margin
explanation: Under Section 64VA of the Insurance Act, 1938 and IRDAI regulations, every insurer must maintain an excess of assets over liabilities known as the Solvency Margin. IRDAI has mandated a 'Control Level of Solvency' ratio of 1.50 (i.e. Available Solvency Margin / Required Solvency Margin ≥ 150%). If it falls below 1.50, the insurer must submit a financial restoration plan.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Insurance Audit - Unearned Premium Reserve (UPR)
question: In the statutory audit of Suraksha General Insurance Ltd. for FY 2023-24, the auditor verifies the Reserve for Unexpired Risks (UPR) under Section 64V of the Insurance Act. For Fire, Marine Cargo, and Miscellaneous insurance policies, what are the statutory minimum percentages of net premium income required to be transferred to the UPR?
options: 50% of Net Premium Income for Fire and Miscellaneous business, and 100% of Net Premium Income for Marine Hull and Marine Cargo business.
25% across all general insurance lines of business.
100% for all policies regardless of line of business.
Zero, because insurance income is recognized on a cash receipt basis under IRDAI.
ref: Section 64V of Insurance Act, 1938 & IRDAI (Preparation of Financial Statements) Regulations
explanation: Under Section 64V of the Insurance Act, 1938 and IRDAI regulations, the reserve for unexpired risks is created at: (a) 50% of net premium income for Fire and Miscellaneous insurance business; and (b) 100% of net premium income for Marine Hull & Marine Cargo insurance business (reflecting longer voyaging risk profiles).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Insurance Audit - Premium Received Before Risk Inception (Section 64VB)
question: Under Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938, what is the statutory prohibition regarding risk assumption by an insurer?
options: No risk can be assumed by the insurer unless and until the premium has been received in advance or guaranteed to be paid in such manner and within such time as prescribed.
Risk may be assumed immediately and premium collected up to 1 year after the policy expires.
Section 64VB only applies to foreign reinsurance companies.
Insurers can waive premium collection entirely for government officials.
ref: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938 - No Risk to be Assumed unless Premium is Received in Advance
explanation: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938 is a strict statutory provision stipulating that no insurer shall assume any risk in respect of any insurance business on which insurance permit is issued unless and until the premium payable is received by him or is guaranteed to be paid by such person in such manner and within such time as may be prescribed.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Government Audit - Constitutional Mandate of C&AG
question: Under Articles 148 to 151 of the Constitution of India and the C&AG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, what is the role and constitutional status of the Comptroller and Auditor General (C&AG) of India?
options: The C&AG is an independent constitutional authority appointed by the President of India who audits all receipts and expenditures of the Government of India, State Governments, and government corporations, and submits audit reports to the President/Governors to be laid before Parliament/State Legislatures.
The C&AG is an executive department under the direct administrative control of the Ministry of Finance.
The C&AG is an internal audit wing of the Reserve Bank of India.
The C&AG's reports are submitted to the Supreme Court for commercial arbitration.
ref: Constitution of India, Articles 148-151 & C&AG DPC Act, 1971
explanation: The C&AG is an independent constitutional authority established under Article 148 of the Constitution of India. Under Article 151, the C&AG submits audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union to the President, who causes them to be laid before each House of Parliament, where they are examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) and Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Government Audit - Propriety Audit
question: In Government Audit, what is the core philosophy and focus of a 'Propriety Audit' conducted by the C&AG?
options: Going beyond mere legal and constitutional regularity to examine whether public expenditure meets standards of financial morality, wisdom, faithfulness, public interest, and avoidance of wasteful extravagance ('Principles of Financial Propriety').
Verifying whether arithmetic additions in government vouchers match mathematical totals.
Auditing private assets and personal bank accounts of government officers.
Checking whether office furniture belongs to the government or is leased.
ref: ICAI CA Final Study Material - Government Audit (Propriety Audit Principles)
explanation: Propriety audit stands for verification of transactions on the touchstone of financial prudence, public interest, and morality. The auditor checks: (1) Whether expenditure is not prima facie more than the occasion demands; (2) Whether an authority exercises the same vigilance as a person of ordinary prudence would exercise in his own case; and (3) That public money is not used for the benefit of a particular person or section.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Section 143(5)-(7) - Audit of Government Companies
question: Under Section 143(5) to 143(7) of the Companies Act, 2013, what is the statutory role of the C&AG in relation to the audit of a Government Company?
options: The C&AG appoints the statutory auditor (chartered accountant), issues directions on the manner of audit, has the right to conduct a supplementary audit within 60 days of the auditor's report, and may cause a test audit to be conducted.
The C&AG conducts the audit personally and private chartered accountants cannot be appointed.
The C&AG only fixes the statutory audit fee and has no right to inspect audit working papers.
The C&AG has no jurisdiction over government companies registered under the Companies Act.
ref: Section 143(5), (6) & (7) of Companies Act, 2013 - Audit of Government Companies
explanation: Under Section 143(5), in the case of a Government company, the C&AG appoints the statutory auditor and directs the manner in which the accounts shall be audited. Under Section 143(6), the C&AG has the right to conduct a supplementary audit of the financial statement within 60 days of receipt of the audit report. Under Section 143(7), the C&AG may cause a test audit to be conducted.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Bank Audit - Non-Fund Based Facilities (LCs and BGs)
question: During statutory branch audit of a bank, how should the auditor verify Non-Fund Based facilities, such as Letters of Credit (LCs) and Bank Guarantees (BGs)?
options: Verify sanction limits, margin money held in term deposits with proper lien marking, underlying trade contracts, expiry dates, invocation tracking, and ensure they are properly disclosed as Contingent Liabilities in Schedule 12 of the Balance Sheet.
Verify them as direct cash advances on the asset side under Schedule 9.
Non-fund based facilities do not carry credit risk and require no audit verification.
Exclude all Bank Guarantees from financial statements unless invoked by court order.
ref: ICAI Guidance Note on Bank Audit - Contingent Liabilities (Schedule 12)
explanation: Non-Fund Based facilities (LCs and BGs) represent off-balance sheet exposures disclosed as Contingent Liabilities under Schedule 12. The auditor must verify sanction terms, adequacy of margin money held with lien marking, validity period, commercial genuineness of underlying transactions, and assess whether any invocation has occurred that crystallizes a direct fund-based liability.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Bank Audit - Agricultural Advances NPA Norms
question: Under RBI guidelines for agricultural advances, when is a crop loan granted for short-duration crops and long-duration crops classified as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA)?
options: For short-duration crops: if the installment of principal or interest remains overdue for 2 crop seasons; For long-duration crops: if the installment remains overdue for 1 crop season.
For all agricultural loans: strictly after 90 days from sanction date.
For all agricultural loans: after 3 consecutive financial years.
Agricultural loans can never be classified as NPAs under Central Government regulations.
ref: RBI Master Circular on IRACP - Agricultural Advances NPA Norms
explanation: Under RBI guidelines, a loan granted for agricultural purposes will be treated as an NPA if: (a) In the case of short-duration crops, the installment of principal or interest remains unpaid for two crop seasons beyond the due date; and (b) In the case of long-duration crops (crops with crop season longer than 1 year), the installment remains unpaid for one crop season beyond the due date.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Insurance Audit - Policyholders' vs Shareholders' Funds
question: In the preparation and audit of insurance companies' financial statements under IRDAI regulations, which two distinct financial accounts must be prepared and kept segregated?
options: Policyholders' Account (Technical Account - Revenue Account Form A-RA / B-RA) determining operating profit/loss of insurance business, and Shareholders' Account (Non-Technical Account - Profit and Loss Account Form A-PL / B-PL).
Cash Account and Bank Account.
Manufacturing Account and Trading Account.
Capital Expenditure Account and Revenue Expenditure Account.
ref: IRDAI (Preparation of Financial Statements and Auditor's Report of Insurance Companies) Regulations, 2002
explanation: Under IRDAI accounting regulations, an insurer must prepare: (1) Revenue Account (Policyholders' Account) separately for each line of business to determine underwriting surplus/deficit; and (2) Profit & Loss Account (Shareholders' Account) which incorporates transfers from the Revenue Account, investment income on shareholders' funds, and non-insurance corporate expenses.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
topicTitle: Audit of Specific Entities: Banks, Insurance Companies, and Government Bodies
